items.title: There’s more to women than sexuality – Bukola Ikuomola
items.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Actress and filmmaker Bukola Ikuomola, popularly known as MZNicollet, has said women should be recognised for their intellect, achievements and contributions to society rather than their sexuality. In a chat with Potpourri, Ikuomola, who expressed her views on women flaunting their sexuality on social media, said she admired women who distinguished themselves through their intelligence and accomplishments. “There is more to women than sexuality. I admire women who are known for their intellect and other great achievements,” she said. The Ondo State-born actress, who also has Urhobo roots in Warri, Delta State, said she developed a passion for acting from an early age and had always admired the profession. She is a graduate of Novena University, Ogume, Delta State, and also runs Nickiscollections as its chief executive officer. Speaking about the sacrifices she has made to build her acting career, Ikuomola said she had invested considerable time, effort and the little money available to her in improving her craft. She described working with veteran actors, including Saheed Balogun, Jobola Dabo, Ayo Mogaji and Muyiwa Ademola, as some of her memorable experiences in the industry. She also expressed pride in producing her first movie, *Enemy Within*. On the kind of roles she enjoys playing, Ikuomola said she preferred heroic characters who demonstrate strength and determination and contribute meaningfully to a story. However, she noted that her versatility allows her to approach different roles with passion. The actress said her ambition was to become a megastar with an international reputation, extending her influence beyond Nollywood. On relationships, Ikuomola said respect and a good sense of humour were qualities she valued in a man, adding that she preferred men to make the first move. She also declared a preference for money over love, explaining that past experiences had left her feeling used in relationships because of how much she gave to the people she loved. “Now I go for money. And if love comes with it, I grab it too,” she said, adding that love becomes sweeter when money is involved. The post There’s more to women than sexuality – Bukola Ikuomola appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: How Real Warri Pikin conquered comedy stages across continents
items.description: By Ayo Onikoyi When Nigerian comedian and actor Anita Alaire Asuoha, popularly known as Real Warri Pikin, won the Best Stand-Up Comedian award at the 2026 African Muzik Magazine Awards (AFRIMMA), it marked another milestone in a career built on hard work, persistence and an unmistakable brand of humour. The honour, presented at the awards ceremony held in Dallas, Texas, on September 12, placed her ahead of several established comedy stars, including Basketmouth, Bovi, Godfrey, Eric Omondi, Trevor Noah, Patrick “Salvado” Idringi and Ty Ngachira. Her victory was a significant recognition of her growing influence in African comedy and her expanding international profile. “This award means a lot to me because it is a recognition of the journey, the work and the years of showing up even when I didn’t know where it would lead,” she said. “To be recognised as Best Comedian at AFRIMMA, representing Nigeria and Africa, is a huge honour. It also reminds me that staying true to who you are and using your story to connect with people can take you places you never imagined,” she added. For Asuoha, the AFRIMMA triumph represents more than a trophy. It reflects years of building an entertainment career that spans stand-up comedy, acting, digital content creation, live shows and television and web productions. Known for her energetic stage presence, Warri-inflected expressions and use of Nigerian Pidgin, Real Warri Pikin has developed a comic identity rooted in everyday experiences, relationships and the peculiarities of Nigerian life. Her ability to turn familiar situations into humorous stories has helped her connect with audiences across different age groups and cultural backgrounds. Her journey from online comedy skits to major entertainment stages has also demonstrated the growing opportunities available to Nigerian comedians who can build audiences through digital platforms and translate that popularity into live performances. One of the defining projects in her career is “Real Warri Pikin Unfiltered”, a comedy show that expanded beyond Nigeria to audiences in Ghana and the United Kingdom, including Milton Keynes, Manchester and London. The show established her ability to headline performances outside her home country while retaining the distinctive humour that first endeared her to Nigerian audiences. She has also performed at established Nigerian comedy platforms and events, including “AY Live”, “Warri Again?” and Bovi’s “Man on Fire”, sharing stages with some of the country’s recognised entertainers. Her international ambitions gathered further momentum in 2026 with the “In My Element” tour. The American leg included performances in Dallas and Houston, Texas, while the Canadian leg covered Winnipeg, Toronto, London, Saskatoon, Regina and Vancouver. The Canadian run was reported as a sold-out six-city tour, underlining her appeal among Nigerians and other African comedy enthusiasts living abroad. The United States shows also featured veteran actor Richard Mofe-Damijo, popularly known as RMD, while Uche Jombo and Chioma Chukwuka were among the Nollywood personalities associated with the tour events. Another major milestone awaits her in London, where she is scheduled to headline *In My Element* at indigo at The O2 on November 29, 2026. The performance is expected to make her the first African female comedian to headline a solo show at the venue, marking a significant moment for Nigerian women in stand-up comedy. Beyond the international tours, Real Warri Pikin has built an impressive record of awards. In 2022, she won Stand-Up Comedian of the Year and Most Creative Comedy Show at The Humour Awards. She also received the Comedy Act of the Year honour at the African Choice Awards that year, consolidating her reputation as one of Nigeria’s leading female comedy performers. Her transition into acting has further widened her entertainment portfolio. She has appeared in Nollywood productions, including *Fate of Alakada*, *Prophetess*, *The Ghost and the Tout Too*, *Merry Men 2* and *Aki and Pawpaw*. These roles have allowed her to extend her comic abilities beyond the stage and social media into mainstream film. On television and digital platforms, she has also explored original storytelling. Her comedy web series *School of Thought*, launched in 2021, featured her as Teacher Afoke and used humour to address issues affecting students and young people. The project was accompanied by a music single featuring singer Teni. In November 2024, she introduced another web series, *Base on Street*, on her YouTube channel. The story follows two sisters who leave Warri for Lagos in search of better opportunities but encounter difficulties as they attempt to establish themselves in the city. Through the series, she combines comedy with social commentary on survival, difficult choices and the risks confronting young people seeking a better life. Her achievements also extend beyond entertainment. Through the Real Warri Pikin Foundation, she has pursued initiatives focused on women, children, education and mental wellness. Her willingness to speak openly about personal challenges has also contributed to conversations about emotional well-being and the importance of seeking support. These different aspects of her career reveal an entertainer who has moved beyond the limits of social media comedy to build a broader presence across live entertainment, film, digital storytelling and social advocacy. The AFRIMMA award therefore arrives at a time when Real Warri Pikin is extending her reach beyond Nigeria through international tours and increasingly ambitious stage productions. Her journey also reflects the potential of Nigerian comedy to travel across borders without losing the local expressions and experiences that give it character. From the comedy stages of Nigeria to audiences in Europe and North America, Asuoha has continued to build on the identity that made her popular. With the AFRIMMA recognition adding to her growing list of honours, her career offers another example of how a distinct Nigerian voice can find an audience far beyond its place of origin. The post How Real Warri Pikin conquered comedy stages across continents appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Mixed reactions trail Zlatan’s wedding
items.description: By Sarah Ammah Nigerian street-pop star Omoniyi Temidayo Raphael, popularly known as Zlatan Ibile, has sparked conversations online following his traditional wedding to his longtime partner, Davita Lamai, in Lagos on October 24, 2026. The glamorous ceremony attracted celebrities, including singer Davido, who served as one of the groomsmen. The couple impressed guests with their traditional outfits and colourful cultural displays, making the celebration a major talking point on social media. While many fans congratulated the couple and praised their outfits, others focused on Davita’s appearance, with some social media users making negative comments about her looks. Another issue that generated debate was Zlatan’s decision to marry Davita after they had already welcomed two children together. Some critics questioned why he chose to marry a woman who already had two children for him, while others defended the couple, arguing that their relationship and decision to marry were nobody else’s business. The wedding also attracted attention following Nollywood actress Joke Jigan’s comments about the absence of popular “Lagos baddies” at the event, which generated mixed reactions online. Despite the criticism, many fans celebrated the couple’s union and praised Zlatan for taking the next step in his relationship with Davita. Ultimately, the wedding became more than a celebration of love, turning into a social media debate about beauty standards, relationships, marriage and public opinion. items.title: Chacx, African China collaborate on ‘Forgive’
items.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Nigerian singer Chacx has collaborated with veteran musician African China on his new single, Forgive, released on Friday, October 30. The collaboration brings the emerging singer together with African China, known for his street-inspired music and socially conscious themes. Speaking about the collaboration, Chacx expressed excitement about working with the veteran singer, describing the experience as an opportunity to learn from an established voice in Nigerian music. “Working with African China is an exciting experience for me. I have great respect for his journey and the connection his music has built with audiences over the years. Collaborating with him gave me an opportunity to exchange creative ideas and approach the song from different perspectives. I believe working with artistes from different generations can broaden your understanding of music and challenge you to grow. I am glad to have him on Forgive and look forward to listeners experiencing what we have created together,” Chacx said. Chacx, whose real name is Manu Charles Chukwuye, began his professional music career in 2019 with Obi Mo, featuring Cme2k. His subsequent releases include the EPs New Beginning (2021) and Advanced (2023), alongside songs such as Blessed, featuring Portable and Shocker Lo Se Beat, Hold Me, Baby Girl, Feelings and Fake Friends. In 2026, he signed with Homeboy International Music Label, adding another development to his career. With Forgive, Chacx brings his sound together with African China’s established musical identity in a collaboration that introduces a new release to both artistes’ catalogues. items.title: Congolese singer Agressivo Nyandoro targets Nigerian market
items.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Congolese singer and songwriter Agressivo Nyandoro has identified Nigeria as one of the African markets he hopes to reach as he seeks to expand his music beyond the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The musician, who began his musical journey as a guitarist in 2009 before releasing his own music in 2012, said he wants his songs to connect with audiences across the continent while retaining the cultural identity that shaped his sound. “Looking ahead, I would like my music to reach more people outside the DRC. Nigeria interests me, as do other African markets where music circulates widely,” Nyandoro said. Known for drawing inspiration from everyday experiences, the Lubumbashi-born musician incorporates storytelling into his songs, exploring human relationships, family responsibilities and social issues. He said his approach to music goes beyond entertainment. “I would simply say that I am a message. When I sing, I am not just trying to make people dance. I also want to tell them something, help them understand a situation, or encourage them to think about what is happening around them,” he said. His song, Jonathan, explores infidelity, an absent husband and the consequences of neglecting family responsibilities. According to the singer, the story reflects situations he has observed in society. Nyandoro is also pursuing cross-border collaborations, having worked with Tanzanian musician Stamina Shorwebwenzi and Shakis Boy on Ipo Siku (Remix). His EP, Déterminé, features Congolese artistes Celeo Scram and Jaysix Abdallah. He believes such collaborations can help African musicians reach audiences beyond their home countries. “An artist from the DRC can reach an audience in Tanzania, just as a Tanzanian artist can introduce their music to Congolese listeners,” he said. Nyandoro is scheduled to perform at Espace Village Chez Ntemba in Kinshasa on October 31, 2026, as he continues working towards expanding his audience. The post Congolese singer Agressivo Nyandoro targets Nigerian market appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Shuga Band immortalises late founder, Akiin Shuga with new innovations
items.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Nigeria’s foremost premium live music ensemble, Shuga Band is marking the first anniversary of its late founder, Akinloye Tofowomo popularly known as Akiin Shuga by reinventing its brand identity with the launch of a new logo asset to immortalize his glorious memory. The band dedicated the entire month of October to celebrate its late founder with the unveiling of the new brand identity across all owned media platforms. It also reinforced her new look identity at all her engagements in the month of October. Signifying professionalism and excellence in music, the new identity carries the face of the widely-regarded founder holding a mic and doing what he knew how to do best for the larger part of his life. Further deepening the legacy, the band released Best of Akiin Shuga on digital platforms, a compilation of his life performances. These deep values have kept the band going for over two and a half decade making it a reference point in the pantheon of live music. The latest effort is another layer to deepen a strong structure around the band in its post-founder phase. While unveiling a Valentine medley for lovers earlier in the year, the band also announced the constitution of a high-calibre advisory board to provide oversight and direction.. Shuga band has been proving doubters wrong and converting them to clients and lovers one show at a time. It continues to enjoy patronage from event planners, vendors and fans alike. Among its recent back-to-back performances include the high-octane 60th birthday shindig of Dr Muiz Banire’s 60th birthday day party, Seplat Nigerian Content Day, Prince Nduka Obaigbena’s 67th birthday, FCMB Sheventures and Shuttlers’s 10th anniversary among a host of others. Still maintaining her founder, Akiin Shuga’s signature music repertoire and flawlessly delivered, the band continues to wow guests. Shuga Band is known for her eclectic sound switching seamlessly among genres such as classics, traditional, gospel and contemporary. “Our founder, Akiin Shuga, taught us that music is service to people, to God and joy itself. He advocated for a structured industry built on integrity, trust and professionalism, and our ability to sustain his legacy is a testament to those values,” says Maria Tofowomo, COO, Shuga Band. Also speaking, Jerry Odeh, Business Manager, “We are grateful for the support that we have enjoyed from all our stakeholders in the last one year. The strong values of service, excellence and professionalism established by our founder and maestro, Akiin Shuga has been our compass. With such a solid legacy backbone, Shuga Band is now being established as a generational brand. We will continue to innovate and ensure effective service delivery for all our stakeholders.” Explaining more, he also revealed that activities of the Shuga Limb Foundation, a passion project of the late founder and anti-polio champion has not stopped making impact. In celebration of World Polio Day, the foundation recently empowered two physically challenged persons. Presented by Kunle Akinkugbe, one beneficiary received shoemaking tool and the other a wheelchair, giving them support for their livelihood and mobility. Established in 1998 by the Berklee College of Music-trained virtuoso, Akinloye Tofowomo, Shuga Band has carved an enduring legacy as one of the few long-serving live entertainment music bands in not only Nigeria but also Africa. Until his unfortunate demise on October 30th 2025, Akiin Shuga as he is fondly called led Shuga Band to entertain the one percent of Nigerian high society at exclusive functions. His prestige audience included three serving Presidents as well as the top five Nigerian billionaires among others. His magical voice and mastery helped cement the place of the former President of the Association of Music Band Owners of Nigeria (AMBON) in the hall of fame. The post Shuga Band immortalises late founder, Akiin Shuga with new innovations appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Enkay Ogboruche wins Africa Gospel Music Impact Award at Clima Awards 2026
items.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Award-winning worship leader and recording artiste Nkiruka Gift Ogboruche, popularly known as Enkay Ogboruche, has been named winner of the Africa Gospel Music Impact Award at the 2026 Clima Awards Africa, held on the 9th of October 2026 in Lagos, Nigeria. The award honours gospel ministers whose sound has crossed borders and shaped worship culture across the continent. It comes at the peak of a landmark year for the singer. Over more than a decade, Enkay has grown from humble beginnings into one of Africa’s most respected worship voices. She has released three albums, *The Kingdom Anthem* (2015), *The Bridge* (2018) and *Declaration* (2023), and has given the global church anthems such as “Yes, You Are The Lord” and “Salute,” the latter featuring Grammy winner Kierra Sheard. Her influence extends well beyond the microphone. She is the convener of Enkay Live in Concert, Pneuma Worship Experience and Alabanza, and the founder of The Spotlight, a platform dedicated to discovering and mentoring the next generation of gospel talent. The latest recognition follows her win as Diaspora Female Artiste of the Year at the 2026 Nigeria International Gospel Music Awards (NIGMA) and her induction into the 2026 new class of the Recording Academy (Grammy), placing her among a growing number of African music professionals shaping global music conversations at the highest level. Enkay has often described her ministry as a blend of discipline, growth and grace, a journey that has taken her from local church platforms to international stages, including Liberty University’s Global Night of Worship alongside Michael W. Smith. Industry watchers say the award is well deserved, citing not only her vocal excellence and consistent hits but also her decade-long commitment to promoting authentic worship and exporting African gospel music to the world. With her fourth album in the works, Enkay Ogboruche continues to show that African gospel music has both the message and the mastery to impact the world. items.title: Ufuoma Okonoko unveils digital strategy to unlock billions for Nigeria’s creative sector
items.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Barrister Ufuoma Okonoko, a digital monetisation expert and Chief Operating Officer of Atlantic World Digital Communications, has unveiled a digital strategy aimed at unlocking billions of dollars in international revenue for Nigeria’s creative sector through strategic distribution, marketing and commercialisation of locally produced content and products. Okonoko, who is also a Nollywood actress and producer known professionally as Angel Ufuoma, said Nigeria’s creative industry holds enormous potential to generate foreign exchange, identifying filmmaking, Afrobeats, fashion, culinary arts, publishing, pharmaceuticals, arts and crafts, and tourism as sectors that could benefit from improved access to international markets. She explained that the strategy informed the development of Blaze Channel, a United States-based digital monetisation platform designed to distribute and generate revenue from Nigerian films while creating international markets for other products and services within the country’s creative economy. According to her, the initiative is intended to address the persistent difficulties filmmakers encounter in generating adequate revenue from their productions, while leveraging the international appeal of Nollywood and Afrobeats to introduce other Nigerian products to global consumers. “Nollywood filmmakers produce great films, but they find it very difficult to monetise them. We created Blaze Channel as a digital monetisation platform in the USA, not only to stream and monetise the movies, but more importantly to monetise Nigerian Creative Industry products,” she said. Okonoko explained that the strategy would use films and music to attract international audiences before introducing them to other Nigerian products, including fashion items, culinary offerings, publishing materials, pharmaceutical products, artificial intelligence solutions, and arts and crafts available for purchase by consumers overseas. She said the approach was designed to go beyond conventional film distribution by creating a broader commercial ecosystem in which Nigerian entertainment content could serve as a gateway for other homegrown businesses seeking access to international markets. According to her, the model could also stimulate interest in Nigeria as a tourism destination and encourage foreign direct investment by exposing international audiences to the country’s cultural assets, creative talent and business opportunities. The company disclosed that Okonoko spent 10 years working with software engineers in the United States to develop the platform before its official launch in 2018. Since then, Blaze Channel has attracted more than 2,000 subscribers worldwide. The company is now seeking additional capital to acquire distribution rights to more Nollywood films and strengthen its marketing budget, steps it considers necessary to expand the platform’s reach and improve its ability to generate revenue from Nigerian creative products in international markets. The Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Atlantic World Digital Communications, Nigerian-American filmmaker Tony Abulu, expressed confidence in Okonoko’s work and the commercial prospects of the initiative. Abulu said he planned to introduce the platform’s concept to American filmmakers and businesses through various American chambers of commerce, a move that could help build partnerships and create further opportunities for the distribution and monetisation of Nigerian content and products. Beyond her digital media venture, Okonoko has established a presence in Nollywood, featuring in more than 40 films. Her acting credits include *Spellbound*, alongside Daniel K. Daniel, Enyinna Nwigwe and Mercy Aigbe; *Superstar*, featuring Tekno Miles, AY, Nyanya and Jide Kosoko; and *Doctor Bello*, written, directed and produced by Abulu. She also featured in *American Japa*, which stars Toyin Abraham, Odunlade Adekola, Kanayo O. Kanayo and veteran actress Tina Amuziam. Her involvement in film production and distribution complements her digital monetisation initiative, which seeks to connect Nigerian entertainment content with audiences beyond the country while exploring additional commercial opportunities for the wider creative industry. The company further indicated that a film titled *Reincarnation – Dance of the Masquerade*, featuring leading Hollywood and Nollywood actors, was in development for 2027. However, details about the production, including its cast and other aspects of the project, were not provided. In another step towards expanding its operations, Blaze Channel has applied to the Creative Economy Development Fund (CEDF). The company hopes that access to funding will support its expansion plans and strengthen its efforts to connect Nigerian creative businesses with international markets. Okonoko identified the African-American consumer market as a significant opportunity for Nigerian businesses, citing the community’s substantial purchasing power and the potential for Nigerian products to attract a share of its spending. “Wait until we truly unleash our monetisation potential of billions of dollars in the African-American community in the USA, where our ‘cousins’ already spend two trillion dollars annually as consumers in America,” she said. She expressed optimism that a well-structured digital monetisation strategy could help Nigeria and other African countries expand the international reach of their creative industries, diversify sources of foreign exchange and attract greater revenue from overseas consumers. The initiative reflects an approach that combines entertainment distribution with broader product marketing, using the global appeal of Nigerian films and music to create commercial opportunities for businesses across several sectors of the economy. However, the projected economic gains will depend on Blaze Channel’s ability to secure distribution rights, attract and retain international audiences, convert viewership into purchases, and establish effective commercial partnerships. Its long-term impact will also depend on the platform’s capacity to scale its subscriber base, sustain marketing efforts and demonstrate that the model can generate consistent revenue for filmmakers and other Nigerian creative businesses. items.title: CONHESS: JOHESU mobilises health workers for showdown with FG
items.description: … Threatens industrial action over 13-year salary adjustment delay By Chioma Obinna The Joint Health Sector Unions (JOHESU) has begun mobilising health workers nationwide for possible industrial action over the Federal Government’s failure to implement the adjustment of the Consolidated Health Salary Structure (CONHESS), a demand that has remained unresolved for about 13 years. The union, which warned that it would resist any attempt to frustrate the salary adjustment, said it was no longer prepared to tolerate further delays in implementing the agreement. This was part of the resolutions reached at an emergency expanded National Executive Council, NEC, virtual meeting held on Thursday, October 29, 2026, attended by its affiliates and organs at federal and state levels. In a resolution jointly signed by the JOHESU National Chairman, Comrade Kabiru Minjibir, and National Secretary, Comrade Martin Egbanubi, JOHESU said the season for uninterrupted implementation of the CONHESS adjustment was now or never, warning that it would not accept threats from what it described as meddlesome interlopers over the welfare and future of health workers. The union recalled that President Bola Tinubu had, on June 5, 2023, promised to actualise the adjustment while appealing to JOHESU to suspend its strike after assuming office. It also recalled that the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare had, on the same date, forwarded the 2021 High Level Body Technical Committee Report on the adjustment to the Budget Office of the Federation, the secretariat of the Presidential Committee on Salaries, PCS. However, JOHESU accused the government of allowing the process to stall behind the inability of the PCS to meet, warning that any further attempt to use the committee’s failure to act as an excuse would be met with resistance. The union commended the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria, TUC, for taking decisive steps towards securing the adjustment, describing it as the oldest demand in organised labour history. It also reminded the Federal Government of the provisions of the Trade Unions Act, Cap T14, LFN, 2004, which permits trade unions to negotiate benefit packages and collective bargaining agreements on behalf of their members. JOHESU consequently placed its members on alert and directed the commencement of mobilisation across health institutions nationwide for possible industrial action and what it described as necessary but unparalleled resistance should the government yield to attempts to frustrate the demand. The union, however, urged members to remain peaceful while awaiting further directives from the NLC and TUC, following the ultimatum and timeline issued to the Federal Government. JOHESU comprises the Medical and Health Workers’ Union of Nigeria, MHWUN; Nigerian Union of Allied Health Professionals, NUAHP; Senior Staff Association of Universities Teaching Hospitals, Research Institutes and Associated Institutions, SSAUTHRIAI; and Non-Academic Staff Union of Educational and Associated Institutions, NASU, including its technical arm, the Assembly of Healthcare Professional Associations, AHPA. The post CONHESS: JOHESU mobilises health workers for showdown with FG appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Cérémonie d’ouverture JOJ Dakar 2026 : Dakar organise, l’Afrique s’illustre
items.description: La cérémonie d’ouverture des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026 a tenu ses promesses. Pour une première organisation sur le sol africain, les attentes étaient particulièrement élevées. Le défi de l'organisation immense. Dakar a répondu présent. Au-delà de la performance artistique, le Comité d’organisation des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (COJOJ) semble avoir fait le choix d’une représentation qui dépasse les seules frontières sénégalaises. Les différentes séquences chorégraphiques ont accordé une place aussi bien aux expressions culturelles du Sénégal qu’à celles des autres pays du continent. Une approche fédératrice qui a permis de célébrer la diversité des cultures, tout en mettant en avant, ce qui rassemble les peuples. À travers les rythmes, les mouvements et les différentes prestations, c’est toute une identité plurielle qui s’est racontée au monde. La créativité et le savoir-faire étaient tout aussi remarquables. Chorégraphies maîtrisées, innovations scénographiques, technologies numériques, jeux de lumière et créations artistiques se sont conjugués pour offrir un spectacle à couper le souffle. Au-delà de l’esthétique, cette représentation a confirmé les capacités techniques, artistiques et organisationnelles mobilisées, pour accueillir un événement de cette envergure. L’histoire et la mémoire collective ont également trouvé échos dans cette narration visuelle, contribuant à valoriser les héritages et à inscrire le spectacle, dans une perspective de transmission. La jeunesse et les générations futures, au cœur même de l’esprit des JOJ, ont bénéficié d’une attention particulière. Elles ont incarné cette ambition de faire du sport un vecteur d’éducation, de rapprochement et d’ouverture sur le monde. Les délégations, les jeunes athlètes, les artistes et les chorégraphes ont ainsi pleinement contribué à donner corps, à une mise en scène où le sport a harmonieusement dialogué avec les identités culturelles. Le spectacle s’est déroulé sous les yeux des plus hautes autorités, avec à leur tête le président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Faye. Une présence à la mesure de la portée historique de ce rendez-vous. Au-delà du cérémonial, cette ouverture aura surtout porté un message, Dakar accueille, le Sénégal organise et l’Afrique s’illustre. O.BA

items.title: Projet ProEmploi+ : 14 personnes en situation de handicap dotées de matériels adaptés à leurs postes de travail
items.description: Agoè-Nyivé, 31 oct. (ATOP) – Quatorze personnes en situation de handicap ont bénéficié de matériels adaptés à leurs postes de travail, le vendredi 30 octobre, dans la préfecture d’Agoè-Nyivé, dans le cadre du projet ProEmploi+, en vue de favoriser leur inclusion professionnelle. Cette initiative est portée par la Fédération togolaise des associations de personnes handicapées (FETAPH), avec l’appui de la coopération allemande, à travers la GIZ, dans le cadre du programme de promotion de l’emploi des femmes et des groupes vulnérables au Togo. Les équipements remis sont notamment composés de mobiliers de bureau ergonomiques, de matériels numériques, d’équipements orthopédiques et d’aides techniques à la mobilité, entre autres, des fauteuils roulants et des cannes. Ils visent à améliorer les conditions de travail des bénéficiaires et à leur permettre d’exercer leurs activités professionnelles dans un environnement adapté à leurs besoins. La cérémonie a également permis de présenter la démarche d’identification des besoins individuels, les objectifs de l’adaptation des postes de travail ainsi que les responsabilités des bénéficiaires en matière d’utilisation, d’entretien et de suivi des équipements reçus. Des témoignages, des échanges interactifs et une présentation des matériels ont marqué la rencontre. Le représentant du ministre chargé de la Solidarité, M. Fiagbé Nukunu Yaovi Edem, a souligné que cette initiative traduit la nécessité de mettre à la disposition de chaque travailleur les moyens nécessaires pour exercer pleinement ses compétences dans des conditions adaptées à ses besoins. Il a indiqué que le gouvernement poursuit ses efforts pour promouvoir les droits des personnes en situation de handicap, notamment en renforçant leur accès et maintien dans l’emploi et leur participation à la vie professionnelle. M. Fiagbé a ajouté que la remise de ces équipements constitue une réponse personnalisée aux besoins des bénéficiaires pour faciliter l’exercice de leurs fonctions. La cheffe du projet ProEmploi+, Mme Whbke Ott, a exprimé sa satisfaction à l’occasion de cette remise officielle de matériels. Elle a souligné que ces équipements contribueront à renforcer leurs capacités et à leur permettre d’être plus performantes dans leurs activités professionnelles. Le président du conseil d’administration de la FETAPH, Akakpo Numado Gratien, a expliqué le processus de sélection des bénéficiaires. Un appel à manifestation d’intérêt destiné aux personnes en situation de handicap exerçant une activité professionnelle et souhaitant bénéficier d’un accompagnement pour gagner en autonomie et en efficacité a été lancé. Les fiches de candidature ont été diffusées à travers le réseau de la fédération. Après réception des candidatures, une commission a étudié les dossiers et sélectionné les bénéficiaires conformément aux critères établis avec la GIZ. Il a salué l’appui de la coopération allemande et assuré que les bénéficiaires sont appelés à faire un bon usage des équipements mis à leur disposition. ATOP/ASA/SED/KYA

items.title: Stable on paper. What about your pocket?
items.description: Dr Mahamudu Bawumia and Hon.Kojo Oppong Nkrumah have raised critical questions about Ghana’s economy. However, the Government is confident in its recovery from the cost-of-living crisis whilst forging a new economic policy initiative worth US$10bn over five years (about GH¢23bn a year). Ghanaians must understand the context when looking at the macroeconomic indicators. Be well informed about the political equalisation in these conversations and ask the critical questions about the outcome, which, ultimately, is: JOBS, GROWTH, UNEMPLOYMENT. This article does exactly 3 things: Peg the macroeconomic data side by side with the statements made Examine the prospects of the Government’s New baby “New Economy” And most importantly, whether the policies and promised 24hr economy have achieved the intended purpose of reducing the unemployment rate And finally, what the state of unemployment looks like, which was the main issue at hand for which this government was voted into power: a promised 3-shift job system that will create employment and expand economic growth in key sectors. Publicly available data show stability: inflation down from 23.8% to 5.2%; debt-to-GDP down from 61.8% to 44.7%; growth at 6%; multidimensional poverty improved by 3 percentage points (21.9%); and the bank lending rate halved (15.6%). One might argue that the current inflation print is somewhat detached from market reality; however, a lower inflation rate does not necessarily mean lower costs of goods and services. According to the Ghana Statistical Service (GSS), the Consumer Price Index as at September 2026, housing, water and energy inflation (10.3%) poses a huge financial burden on the ordinary Ghanaian. The double-digit inflation (10.3%) simply means the rent, electricity and water bills are hurting the pockets of consumers the most amongst other items in the consumer basket. Government’s Growth figures, as reported in the 2026 Mid-Year Budget review, show Ghana’s Growth stands at 6%; farm growth has halved, from 7.1% to 3.9%, while services grew by 8% in 2026, down from 8.1% in 2025. The positives extend to a poverty reduction of 3 percentage points and the cost of borrowing. However, the Growth figures do not reflect majorly in job creation, as youth unemployment currently stands at 32.4%, most precise, 1 out of 3 young job seekers have no work. This begs the question: of roughly GH¢650bn budgeted over 2 years, and the GH¢1.6bn investment in flagship jobs and social schemes in 2026. Are they yielding the necessary outcomes? Could this be the possible concern fundamental to Dr Bawumia’s assertion of a Paper Economy to Hon. Oppong Nkrumah’s quest for accountability on policy outcomes estimated at GH¢650bn? One could mention that Policy lags, under-execution and release lags are fundamental constraints to the transmission effect of these investments; however, the macroeconomic data. In response to the growth figures and the major concern on jobs, now comes the government’s big bet, “The New Economy”: moving from stability to increasing growth in the economy, mainly to create jobs. The President says US$10bn over five years (about GH¢23bn a year), with an ambitious statement: “We are not going to borrow money for the New Economy Policy… this is our own money.” However, this year alone, reports from the 2026 budgets and the Mid-review indicate that wages, interest and earmarked funds already take 79% of 2026 revenue (GH¢212bn). That leaves GH¢56bn for goods, services and all projects, and in 2026 the prospective New Economy of 2027 would have equalled 41% of it. In perspective, what would funding it mean? New taxes, a tightened revenue mobilisation strategy, or domestic borrowing (bonds)? The 2026 budget already plans GH¢72bn of borrowing at home. But would that be what the President’s statement on “No borrowing for New Economy” means: domestic borrowing and not external borrowing? A masterstroke for funding the New Economy will be a strong revenue mobilisation exercise to meet revenue targets. The lazy approach could be a hike in taxes. As already noted, revenue was GH¢1.4bn short in the first half, with oil revenue 31% below target. One can only be optimistic about revenue performance for 2027. The other downside risk remains the volatility of international commodity prices, especially for Ghana’s exports such as gold, which accounts for 68% of exports and how a projected fall can offset Ghana’s foreign earnings. From March to August 2026, Gold prices fell by 9.1%; the World Bank projects lower prices in 2027, and this risk weighs on Ghana’s fiscal position, as GH¢58bn of bonds fall due in 2027, the same year the New Economy starts. In the world of political equalisation, whataboutism and ‘JANDAMism’, many conversations will arise. For you as a young person, a parent and a business owner, there are 4 key data points to watch: |JOBS| 32.4% Youth unemployment Unemployment has reduced by only 0.1 percentage point and currently stands at 13.0% (end of year 2024 to Q3 2025): 13.1% to 13.0% end of year. Youth unemployment for young persons within the ages of 15-24 remains relatively high at 32.4%. This indicator is a critical outcome of job creation and expansion. |CREDIT| 15.6% lending rate According to the September 2026 press release by the Bank of Ghana, the cost of borrowing has reduced to 15.6%, a 14.6 percentage point reduction in previous rate of 30.2% in 2025. Availability of funds from the banks to the customers including businesses and private citizens, has increased from 1.7% in 2025 to 29% in 2026. |FARMS AND FACTORIES| 3.9% farm growth Sector growth in agriculture has not seen improved growth as it grew at 3.9% compared to a 6.8% growth the previous turn. Agriculture remains a key sector of development , jobs and livelihood for the rural communities. It remains the engine sector to boost job creation and enhance development in rural areas. Its inconsistent underinvestment and lagging growth figures point to the fundamental structural defects in our economy and job creation. |GOLD AND CEDI| GH¢11.55 per US$ Gold prices under various transformations of the Gold for Reserve Program to the Ghana Accelerated National Reserve Accumulation Programme (GANRAP) and Operationalization of the then Precious Minerals Marketing Company (PMMC) to now, GOLDBod. It remains a major export earner to reduce pressure on foreign currencies and to build the reserves to absorb external pressure on the domestic currency. However, its impact relies on an optimal exchange rate and a positive trade balance: A position that improves export earnings without aggressively affecting local businesses through a relatively increased penchant for imports. The reality check is YOU. Is money moving out of your pocket quickly? Money dey pocket?

items.title: From stability to transformation: 5 tests for Ghana’s 2027 Budget
items.description: Ghana is preparing a budget with a different promise. After years of debt restructuring and spending restraint, the government wants to turn economic stability into jobs, investment and higher production. But the repayments coming due in 2027 will compete for the same public money. The International Monetary Fund (IMF) completed the final review of Ghana’s US$3 billion Extended Credit Facility in July. Its successor, the Policy Coordination Instrument, provides monitoring without new financing. The coming budget must show how Ghana intends to sustain its recovery while paying for its next phase of development. There are gains to protect. September inflation was 5.2%, while provisional public debt stood at 45% of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in June. But these figures cannot tell us whether new investments will deliver or how comfortably government can meet its repayments. Judge the budget by how convincingly it links its promises to financing and results. Five tests matter. 1. Show how the New Economy will be financed The published Fiscal Strategy Document proposes investment equivalent to 1.5% of GDP annually for four years, approximately US$10 billion. It identifies two sources of financing: an additional 0.5% of GDP in revenue and room created by reducing the primary surplus. The budget must now show what the money will be used for. Which projects are ready to begin? Who will implement them, and when should the public expect results? A programme intended to create jobs needs measurable employment and production targets alongside its costs. Any private investment expected to follow should be distinguished from money government has actually committed, with public guarantees disclosed. 2. Explain the safeguards behind the lower surplus The government proposes lowering the primary surplus on a commitment basis from 1.5% to 0.5% of GDP from 2027. A primary surplus is the excess of revenue over spending before interest payments. Reducing it leaves more room for expenditure, but also means a smaller contribution towards containing debt, other things being equal. Productive projects can justify greater investment. The harder task is selecting those projects and protecting the budget if expected revenue fails to arrive. Government should explain how the proposed target fits the applicable fiscal rules, what safeguards accompany it, and which spending would be reconsidered if conditions deteriorate. Independent scrutiny by the Fiscal Council would help establish confidence in those choices. 3. Prepare for the repayments coming due The repayment calendar is demanding. Government has announced GH¢58 billion of Domestic Debt Exchange Programme bond maturities in 2027 and another GH¢53 billion in 2028. A reassuring debt ratio does not remove the need to find money when bondholders are owed it. Building a Sinking Fund is therefore reasonable. Government reported GH¢15.6 billion accumulated by 22 July, while the Institute for Fiscal Studies questioned its treatment in the approved budget. The next budget should reconcile the fund’s opening balance, inflows, withdrawals and planned repayments. It should distinguish money saved from money borrowed to build a buffer. Borrowing ahead of maturity can ease immediate pressure, but it brings interest costs and another repayment date. 4. Show whether spending restraint is delaying delivery Preparing for repayments must also leave room to deliver today’s budget. The Ministry of Finance reports a first-half primary surplus of 0.9% of GDP on a commitment basis. Yet capital spending was 39.3% below plan, while net arrears clearance reached only 38.2% of the programmed amount. The improved balance deserves recognition; the shortfalls deserve explanation. Delayed payment of old arrears does not itself explain a commitment-basis surplus. Nevertheless, unfinished projects and overdue bills have consequences beyond the fiscal tables. Contractors waiting for payment may struggle to pay suppliers and workers. Communities waiting for infrastructure continue to bear the cost of its absence. Government should show what it committed to spend, what it paid and what remains overdue. Where spending fell below plan, the explanation should distinguish genuine savings, rejected claims and delays in delivery. Spending less is not automatically evidence of failure, neither is it sufficient evidence of efficiency. 5. Show what public liabilities could cost taxpayers Even a well-executed budget can be disrupted by obligations elsewhere in the public sector. The Fiscal Strategy Document already includes a Fiscal Risk Statement. The budget should build on it by showing how much major exposures could cost taxpayers, when support might be required and who is responsible. Energy-sector obligations, guarantees, gold-purchase operations and central-bank recapitalisation need clear treatment. The IMF’s July review recorded a waiver linked to cost-sharing under the domestic gold purchase programme and reaffirmed the commitment to recapitalise the Bank of Ghana by 2032. These issues need an explanation of their cost and financing. Liabilities already included in public debt should be distinguished from claims that might become government obligations, so that disclosure neither hides exposures nor counts them twice. Before election pressures intensify The 2028 election-year budget will be presented in late 2027. The coming budget is therefore an opportunity to establish safeguards before political spending pressures intensify. Its credibility will depend on what happens after the speech: whether projects progress, payments arrive and emerging risks are reported promptly. None of these asks for less ambition. It asks government to cost its promises, explain its fiscal choices, prepare for repayments and account for delivery. Ghana’s next phase of development needs a budget that connects ambition to evidence. It should survive an audit. Daniel is a PhD student in Accounting at the Muma College of Business, University of South Florida, a qualified Chartered Accountant (ICAG) and Chartered Management Accountant (CIMA). He previously worked as a financial analyst at Deloitte.

items.title: Tour du Faso : L’Algérie roule plus vite à Koudougou
items.description: La 2 e étape du tour du Faso, s’est disputée ce samedi 31 octobre 2026, entre la capitale Ouagadougou et la ville de Koudougou. Hamza Yacine de l’Algérie a été le premier à franchir la ligne. Il a avalé les 129,75 km en 3h21min27s, avec une vitesse moyenne de 38,645 km/h. Le Burkinabè Paul Daumont est le 3 e à franchir la ligne d’arrivée. Le maillot jaune reste toujours sur les épaules du Néerlandais Wijfje Tom. Le départ réel de cette étape, est donnée devant l'ENAREf à 8h24mn avec 78 coureurs de 14 équipes. À l’issue de l’étape de la veille, on note deux (02) abandons. À peine lâché, une échappée de deux (02) Burkinabè est lancée à l'intérieur de Ouagadougou. Les auteurs de cette échappée matinale sont Issouf Ilboudo et Idrissa Ouangrawa et ils possèdent 2mn12s sur le peloton. Au poste de péage de Tintilou, les deux (02) fuyards sont toujours en tête à 1mn30s. Le premier sprint intermédiaire à Kokologho est remportée par Idrissa Ouangrawa, qui est suivi de Issouf Ilboudo. Le Sud Africain Emile Van Niekerk est 3 e . L’échappée sera rattrapée juste après le sprint intermédiaire de Sabou. Sprint remporté d’ailleurs par Idrissa Ouangrawa. Il est suivi par Issouf Ilboudo et le 3 e est Riahi Anes de l’Algérie. C’est groupé que les coureurs rentrent dans la cité du cavalier rouge. Et comme il fallait s’y attendre, c’est au sprint que Hamza Yacine tire dans ses dernières énergies et traverse la ligne le premier. Il est suivi de son compatriote Assal Mohamed Nadib. Paul Daumont est le 3 e à traverser la ligne d’arrivée. Au classement général, Wijfje Tom le Néerlandais est toujours maillot jaune. Son challenger direct est Souleymane Koné du Burkina Faso, qui est à 08 secondes du Néerlandais. Le Sud Africain Basson Gustav est au bas du podium à 10 secondes du maillot jaune. Paul Daumont est 4 e et à 50 secondes du leader. Ce dimanche, la caravane quitte Koudougou pour Boromo avec une distance de 158,90 km. Il est prévu trois (03) sprints intermédiaires à Sabou, Tita et Laba. items.title: Master en Psychologie sur la Prison de haute sécurité de Ouagadougou: Derrière les murs, les blessures invisibles du terrorisme
items.description: Sayouba Pagbelguem, Contrôleur de la Garde de sécurité pénitentiaire (GSP) et chef du Service Suivi Psychologique de la Prison de haute sécurité (PHS) de Ouagadougou, a brillamment soutenu, vendredi 30 octobre 2026, à l’Université Joseph-Ki-Zerbo de Ouagadougou, son mémoire de Master en psychologie clinique et psychopathologie, sanctionné par la mention Très Bien. À travers l’étude du stress post-traumatique chez deux condamnés pour faits de terrorisme, il met en lumière les enjeux psychologiques de la réinsertion sociale et préconise une prise en charge individualisée, pluridisciplinaire et mieux structurée en milieu carcéral. Derrière les portes verrouillées de la Prison de haute sécurité (PHS) de Ouagadougou, certaines blessures ne se voient pas. Elles troublent le sommeil, ravivent des souvenirs douloureux et fragilisent les relations sociales. Ces souffrances psychologiques, susceptibles de compliquer la réinsertion, constituent le cœur de la recherche de Sayouba Pagbelguem. Dans un Burkina Faso confronté aux violences terroristes depuis 2015, son étude explore une dimension importante de la détention : les conséquences psychologiques des événements traumatiques vécus ou auxquels les personnes ont été exposées. Le mémoire, intitulé « Stress post traumatique et réinsertion sociale des condamnés terroristes à la Prison de Haute Sécurité de Ouagadougou », se situe au croisement de la santé mentale, de la sécurité pénitentiaire et de l’accompagnement des détenus. Comprendre le traumatisme pour mieux réinsérer Le choix du sujet répond à une préoccupation clinique et institutionnelle. Selon la présentation du mémoire, les consultations à la PHS sont notamment motivées par des conduites suicidaires et des difficultés relationnelles associées au trouble de stress post-traumatique (TSPT). La question centrale consiste à comprendre les manifestations de ce trouble et les formes de prise en charge psychosociale susceptibles de soutenir la réinsertion. Pour analyser cette problématique, Sayouba Pagbelguem mobilise trois approches théoriques complémentaires : la théorie du traumatisme, les approches cognitivo-comportementales et la théorie de l’attachement. Elles permettent respectivement d’éclairer les conséquences des événements traumatiques, les mécanismes de maintien des symptômes et le rôle potentiel des liens affectifs et sociaux dans le rétablissement. Sur le plan méthodologique, l’étude repose sur deux cas sélectionnés par échantillonnage raisonné, avec la participation volontaire de deux détenus désignés sous les noms d’emprunt de Saadou, 28 ans, et de Tinga, 33 ans. Le chercheur a combiné un guide d’entretien, une grille d’observation clinique et l’échelle PCL-5. Les données recueillies ont fait l’objet d’une analyse thématique et d’une analyse descriptive des scores. Les résultats indiquent des scores PCL-5 de 64 pour Saadou et de 60 pour Tinga. Les manifestations rapportées comprennent des reviviscences, des conduites d’évitement, des altérations négatives des pensées et de l’humeur, de l’hypervigilance et des troubles du sommeil. Des céphalées, des douleurs, des palpitations et des difficultés relationnelles sont également relevées. Ces constats soulignent l’intérêt d’un accompagnement psychologique adapté, sans permettre de généraliser les résultats à l’ensemble des détenus ni d’établir une relation causale entre les symptômes et les difficultés de réinsertion. Une prise en charge pluridisciplinaire comme perspective L’un des apports du mémoire réside dans l’identification des ressources susceptibles de favoriser la stabilité psychosociale. La prise en charge présentée associe interventions psychologiques, soins médicaux, suivi psychiatrique et soutien social. Elle s’appuie également sur le rétablissement des liens familiaux, la formation, les activités professionnelles, le sport, l’alphabétisation et les activités socioculturelles ou spirituelles. Dans les deux cas étudiés, la participation à ces activités est associée à une amélioration rapportée de la stabilité psychosociale. La réinsertion apparaît ainsi comme un processus multidimensionnel qui dépasse l’occupation du détenu ou l’acquisition de compétences professionnelles. Pour la PHS et l’administration pénitentiaire en général, le chercheur formule quatre recommandations : instaurer un dépistage régulier du TSPT, formaliser une prise en charge pluridisciplinaire assortie d’un plan individualisé de réinsertion, restaurer les liens familiaux et mettre en place un suivi-évaluation associant des indicateurs de santé mentale et de réinsertion. La concrétisation de ces propositions suppose une meilleure coordination entre personnels pénitentiaires, psychologues, professionnels de santé et intervenants sociaux. Elle nécessite aussi des ressources adaptées, dans un contexte marqué, selon le mémoire, par le manque de psychologues et de moyens. Le chercheur reconnaît les limites de son dispositif : deux cas permettent une analyse approfondie, mais ne suffisent ni à généraliser les conclusions ni à démontrer l’efficacité causale des interventions. Des recherches complémentaires seront donc nécessaires pour approfondir ces résultats. Présidé par Dr Rasmata Bakyono/Nabaloum, le jury comprenait Pr Aboubacar Barry et Pr Daouda Kouma, codirecteurs du mémoire, ainsi que Dr Alex Nébié, membre critique. La mention Très Bien vient couronner ce travail qui rappelle que sécurité pénitentiaire et accompagnement psychosocial peuvent être complémentaires. Derrière les murs, reconnaître les traumatismes et y répondre avec méthode constitue une piste importante pour concilier sécurité, dignité humaine et perspectives de reconstruction individuelle. Donatien FOFANA, Pour Netafrique.net L’article Master en Psychologie sur la Prison de haute sécurité de Ouagadougou: Derrière les murs, les blessures invisibles du terrorisme est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Le PLFR 2026 adopté par les députés: la ministre des Finances fixe le cap de la rigueur et de la souveraineté budgétaire
items.description: Devant une Assemblée nationale pleinement mobilisée depuis le lancement des travaux le 26 octobre dernier, la ministre de l’Économie, des Finances et du Budget, Mariama Ciré Sylla, a acté une étape décisive pour les finances publiques de la Guinée lors de l'adoption du projet de loi de finances rectificative (PLFR) pour l'exercice 2026. Dans une intervention saluant la qualité du travail parlementaire matérialisé par plus d'une centaine de questions de fond et un rapport touffu, la cheffe du département économique a souligné la synergie retrouvée entre le contrôle législatif et l'action gouvernementale au service de l'intérêt général. Au cœur de ce collectif budgétaire figure une revalorisation nette des ambitions financières du pays. Les prévisions de recettes de l'État s'établissent désormais à 60 000 milliards de francs guinéens, contre 55 858 milliards dans la loi de finances initiale, soit une progression de 7,53 %. Ce résultat, attribué au travail des régies financières (Impôts, Douanes, Trésor, Patrimoine et Investissements privés), s'appuie sur une accélération de la digitalisation, la lutte contre la fraude et une meilleure équité devant l'impôt. En parallèle, une revue menée dans plus de quinze ministères permettra de formaliser et de sécuriser le reversement direct au Trésor des recettes non fiscales ou informelles via des arrêtés d'harmonisation. Aligné sur les inquiétudes des députés quant à l'impact des exonérations fiscales, le ministère finalise une révision des dépenses fiscales pour s'assurer que le secteur minier contribue équitablement au budget national. De nouveaux équipements de contrôle douanier ont été déployés et d'autres sont commandés afin de vérifier scientifiquement les volumes et la qualité des minerais exportés. Face aux retards d'exécution de certains projets financés sur ressources extérieures, Mariama Ciré Sylla a prôné une tolérance zéro envers l'inefficacité administrative. Rappelant qu'« un financement signé n'est pas encore une route construite », elle a annoncé des inspections ciblées sur le terrain, assorties d'un calendrier strict de levée des blocages. Une attention particulière est portée au Port autonome de Conakry, avec un plan visant la clarification des redevances portuaires et le déploiement de mesures durables de désengorgement. Sur le plan social et économique, le PLFR 2026 intègre une provision massive de 913 milliards de francs guinéens destinée à stabiliser les prix des produits pétroliers et à prémunir le pouvoir d'achat des ménages contre les chocs extérieurs. Cette mesure s'accompagne d'un soutien soutenu au secteur privé et d'une révision à venir de la mercuriale des prix pour encadrer le coût des marchés publics. Enfin, sur le volet de la gouvernance interne, le ministère généralise l'outil informatique du Trésor permettant de traiter les factures en 48h et de tracer leur parcours jusqu'à la Banque Centrale. L'opérationnalisation de la « clinique des dossiers » permettra de réunir régulièrement les départements sectoriels pour débloquer les paiements en souffrance. S'engageant à fournir des réponses écrites documentées aux questions techniques restantes, la ministre a réaffirmé sa volonté de maintenir un dialogue permanent et transparent avec la représentation nationale tout au long de l'exécution budgétaire.

items.title: PLFR 2026 : le budget rectifié à 60 064 Mds GNF adopté par les députés sous le sceau de Simandou 2040
items.description: Les députés à l’Assemblée nationale lors de la plénière, ce samedi 31 octobre 2026, après des semaines de débats intenses en commission sous l’œil des régies financières, ont voté à l'unanimité le Projet de Loi de Finances Rectificative (PLFR) 2026 qui traduit l'ajustement des curseurs macroéconomiques du pays face aux soubresauts géopolitiques mondiaux. Entre hausse des recettes à 60 064,47 milliards GNF, maîtrise de l'inflation à 5,2 % et impératifs de transparence fiscale, le texte entérine les grands arbitrages de l’État. Selon le rapport lu par le rapporteur général de l’Assemblée nationale, N'Gouamou Fabara Koné, des agrégats macroéconomiques réajustés Les travaux menés par la Commission des Affaires Économiques et Financières du Parlement mettent en lumière une révision de l’objectif de croissance du Produit Intérieur Brut (PIB), ramené de 9,5 % (initialement prévus en LFI) à 8,6 %. Le PIB nominal s’ajuste quant à lui à 392 503 milliards GNF (contre 401 670 milliards GNF). Du côté de l’inflation, le taux est revu à la hausse à 5,2 % (contre 3,5 % escomptés), tandis que le taux de change s’établit à 8 710 GNF pour un dollar américain. Malgré un taux de pression fiscale projeté à 14,23 % du PIB (contre 12,13 % en LFI), le déficit budgétaire affiche une légère embellie, ramené à -2,01 % du PIB. Une dynamique de recettes portée à 60 064 milliards GNF. Globalement, les prévisions de recettes de l’État affichent une hausse substantielle de 7,53 %, s’établissant à 60 064,47 milliards GNF contre 55 858,10 milliards GNF dans la loi initiale. Cette enveloppe se compose de deux grands blocs : Le budget général : Évalué à 57 664,90 milliards GNF (en progression de 7,92 %), il est dynamisé par l’accroissement des impôts sur les biens et services (+5 340,59 milliards GNF) et sur le commerce extérieur (+1 248,55 milliards GNF). A l'inverse, on note un repli de certains impôts directs sur les revenus et bénéfices (-584,06 milliards GNF). Les Budgets d’Affectation Spéciale (BAS) : Évalués à 2 399,57 milliards GNF, soit 3,99 % du total des recettes. Pour amortir les chocs sociaux, le budget rectifié intègre des mesures fortes : la prise en charge des pertes de recettes pétrolières pour maintenir le carburant à 12 000 GNF à la pompe, l’allocation d'une provision de 913 milliards GNF dédiée à la stabilisation des prix, ainsi que le renforcement des emprunts obligataires (+1 089,84 milliards GNF) et des titres d’État (+1 000 milliards GNF).

items.title: Boubacar Yacine à la FEPAP-Gui : «votre fédération est un œuf. Il peut se casser à tout moment si…»
items.description: Recevant, vendredi 30 octobre 2026, les responsables de la Fédération patronale des professionnels des médias de Guinée (FEPAP-GUI) au siège de la Haute Autorité de la Communication (HAC), son président, Boubacar Yacine Diallo, les a exhortés à préserver leur unité et à surmonter leurs divergences. Pour illustrer la fragilité de leur nouvelle organisation, il a lancé un avertissement sans détour : « Votre fédération est un œuf. Il peut se casser à tout moment si… » Dans son intervention, le président de la HAC a insisté sur les risques que les rivalités internes et les antagonismes professionnels font peser sur la cohésion de la jeune fédération. « Votre fédération est un œuf. Il y a du blanc, il y a du jaune. Mais quand vous le prenez comme œuf, il est fragile. Il peut se casser à tout moment. Il peut y avoir des velléités entre vous, des antagonismes entre vous. C’est ce qu’il faut éviter », a-t-il prévenu. Boubacar Yacine Diallo a ensuite invité les responsables de la FEPAP-GUI à faire preuve de solidarité et à ne pas se laisser entraîner dans des conflits susceptibles de fragiliser leur organisation, qu'ils soient d'origine interne ou extérieure. « Si vous réussissez à transcender tous les conflits qui peuvent surgir en votre sein et des conflits qui sont transportés du dehors pour vous faire éclater, vous gagnerez », a-t-il insisté. Pour étayer son propos, le président de la HAC s'est appuyé sur son expérience à la tête de plusieurs organisations professionnelles, notamment l'Association guinéenne des éditeurs de la presse indépendante (AGUIPEL), l'Union des radiodiffusions et télévisions libres de Guinée (URTELGUI) et la Maison de la presse. Subvention aux médias : pour une répartition plus équitable Au-delà de la cohésion de la fédération, le président de la HAC a abordé les difficultés économiques auxquelles sont confrontées les entreprises de presse. Il a plaidé pour une répartition de la subvention publique qui tienne davantage compte des capacités réelles de production et de fonctionnement des différents médias. « Que ceux qui méritent plus gagnent plus. Que ceux qui méritent moins gagnent moins et ceux qui ne méritent rien, qu’ils aient rien », a-t-il recommandé. Cette position traduit sa volonté de voir les ressources allouées aux médias distribuées selon des critères de mérite et de performance, plutôt que de manière uniforme. Convention collective et autorégulation Boubacar Yacine Diallo a également insisté sur l'urgence de faire avancer le processus de signature de la convention collective des professionnels des médias et de rendre opérationnel l'Observatoire de l'autorégulation des médias. Il souhaite que cette dernière structure soit mise en place avant la fin du mois de novembre. Pour le président de la HAC, l'autorégulation constitue un levier essentiel pour responsabiliser les professionnels, prévenir les manquements et protéger les journalistes ainsi que leurs entreprises contre les conséquences des dérives professionnelles. Enfin, il a réaffirmé la disponibilité de la HAC à accompagner les démarches de la nouvelle fédération et à soutenir les recommandations qu'elle formulera auprès des interlocuteurs concernés.

items.title: Ghana courts Qatari investors into key sectors of economy
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Investment Promotion Authority (GIPA), Simon Madjie, has called for increased investment from Qatar into strategic sectors of Ghana’s economy to strengthen bilateral economic relations and promote sustainable growth. According to him, Ghana was seeking to deepen investment cooperation with Qatar by creating opportunities for partnerships across sectors, including agriculture, manufacturing, energy, infrastructure, financial services, tourism and the creative arts. In an interview with Doha News in Qatar, Mr Madjie said improved air connectivity between the two countries would facilitate business engagements, promote trade and boost investment flows. He was speaking on the sidelines of the ninth edition of the World Investment Forum 2026, hosted by the State of Qatar in partnership with UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD) under the theme, “Investing in the Future.” Mr Madjie said Ghana is keen on attracting Qatari investment into manufacturing, agro-processing, financial services, fintech, digital services, oil and gas, power generation, mining and tourism. He also highlighted opportunities for cooperation in culture and the creative arts, adding that Ghana was interested in leveraging Qatar’s expertise to support the development of industries and strengthen business partnerships. On the investment climate, Mr Madjie said Ghana was working to improve the business environment and create favourable conditions for capital inflows. He pointed out thst the country offered incentives for investors seeking to operate in free zones, as well as incentives relating to factories, equipment and machinery. Mr Madjie said Ghana’s participation in the forum was aimed at showcasing the country’s investment potential and encouraging Qatari businesses to explore commercially viable opportunities. He called for stronger cooperation between the public and private sectors of both countries to establish sustainable partnerships that would serve their mutual interests.

items.title: LFR 2026 : après deux rejets en commission, le texte revient en plénière le 3 novembre
items.description: Le projet de loi n°40/2026 portant loi de finances rectificative (LFR) revient devant l’Assemblée nationale, mardi 3 novembre 2026, à 10 heures, pour son examen en séance plénière. Une étape décisive, après deux rejets successifs en Commission des finances et du Contrôle budgétaire, qui font planer l’incertitude sur l’issue du vote. Le bras de fer entre l’exécutif et la majorité parlementaire de PASTEF-Les Patriotes a véritablement éclaté lors de l’examen du texte, entamé le 20 octobre. À l’issue de plusieurs heures de discussions, le groupe parlementaire avait fait état de désaccords persistants avec le gouvernement, malgré quelques compromis. Les divergences portaient notamment sur les arbitrages budgétaires, les modalités de financement et les garanties attendues par les députés. Dans un communiqué publié le 20 octobre, le groupe avait reconnu l’absence de consensus global et solide. La première sanction est tombée le 23 octobre. La Commission des finances a rejeté le projet de LFR dans son intégralité, ainsi que les deux amendements proposés par le gouvernement. Une déconvenue qui a conduit le Premier ministre à défendre les choix budgétaires de l’exécutif, le 25 octobre, et à appeler les parlementaires à formuler des propositions concrètes. Le gouvernement a ensuite sollicité, en séance plénière le 27 octobre, un renvoi du texte en commission, sur le fondement de l’article 84 du règlement intérieur, afin de poursuivre les discussions. L’Assemblée nationale a également demandé des informations complémentaires. Mais cette nouvelle tentative de rapprochement n’a pas permis de débloquer la situation. Réunie le 30 octobre, après avoir reçu un mémorandum de la commission et des éclaircissements sur les subventions énergétiques, les bourses de sécurité familiale et les dépenses prioritaires, l’équipe du ministre Cheikh Diba a essuyé un deuxième rejet. Les explications fournies par le ministère n’ont donc pas suffi à convaincre les députés. L’exécutif insiste sur la continuité de l’action publique Malgré ces difficultés, l’exécutif entend maintenir le cap. Lors du Conseil des ministres du 28 octobre 2026, le président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, a insisté sur la nécessité d’assurer la continuité des pouvoirs publics. Il a, dans ce sens, demandé au Premier ministre de prendre les dispositions juridiques nécessaires à la mise en œuvre des politiques publiques inscrites dans les projets de loi de finances rectificative pour 2026 et de loi de finances pour 2027. Cette instruction présidentielle traduit la volonté de l’exécutif de préserver la continuité de l’action gouvernementale dans un contexte marqué par les désaccords autour du budget rectificatif. Elle intervient alors que le texte doit encore franchir l’étape décisive de la séance plénière. Le rejet en commission ne préjuge pas automatiquement de l’issue du vote en séance publique. Mais, au regard des positions exprimées jusqu’ici, un nouveau désaveu parlementaire reste possible. Le gouvernement parviendra-t-il à obtenir l’adoption de son texte ou devra-t-il essuyer un troisième revers ? Réponse mardi à l’Assemblée nationale. C.G. DIOP
